# ankra_stack_backup_protection (Resource)

Protects a stack into a backup vault on a schedule: the backup policy on the stack, the counterpart of `ankra cluster stacks protect`. Every change rewrites the whole policy. Destroying the resource unprotects the stack (`ankra cluster stacks unprotect`); restore points already taken are kept. The stack itself stays owned by `ankra_cluster` or the GitOps repository, which leave a stack's policy alone when they do not name one. The platform reports the vault and schedule back, so a change to either outside Terraform plans a correction; `retention` and `selection` are not reported back.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ankra_stack_backup_protection" "shop" {
  cluster_id = "0b6f1d2e-1111-4222-8333-944445555666"
  stack_name = "shop"
  vault      = ankra_backup_vault.production.id
  schedule   = "0 1 * * *"

  retention = {
    daily   = 7
    weekly  = 4
    monthly = 6
  }

  selection = {
    persistent_volume_claims = ["shop/uploads"]
  }

  backup_now = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Identifier of the cluster. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `stack_name` (String) Name of the stack to protect. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `vault` (String) Backup vault the restore points are written to, by name or id (for example `ankra_backup_vault.this.id`).

### Optional

- `backup_now` (Boolean) Take the first restore point when the resource is created instead of waiting for the schedule. Only read on create: changing it later sends nothing and takes no restore point.
- `retention` (Attributes) How many restore points each tier keeps. Unset keeps every restore point. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--retention))
- `schedule` (String) `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly` or a five-field cron expression. Unset, the platform default (daily) applies.
- `selection` (Attributes) Which of the stack's data the restore points carry. Unset, databases are captured and no volume is. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--selection))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<cluster_id>/<stack_name>`.
- `protection_state` (String) The stack's backup posture: `protected`, `unprotected` (for example while the vault is not ready) or `unknown`.
- `vault_name` (String) Name of the vault the policy names.

<a id="nestedatt--retention"></a>
### Nested Schema for `retention`

Optional:

- `daily` (Number) Daily restore points kept. 0 or unset disables the tier.
- `hourly` (Number) Hourly restore points kept. 0 or unset disables the tier.
- `minimum_age` (String) Age below which no restore point is pruned, for example `72h`.
- `minimum_count` (Number) Restore points always kept, whatever their age. 0 or unset disables the tier.
- `monthly` (Number) Monthly restore points kept. 0 or unset disables the tier.
- `weekly` (Number) Weekly restore points kept. 0 or unset disables the tier.
- `yearly` (Number) Yearly restore points kept. 0 or unset disables the tier.


<a id="nestedatt--selection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `selection`

Optional:

- `confirm_exclude_databases` (Boolean) Acknowledges that restore points carry no database contents when `databases` is `false`.
- `databases` (Boolean) Whether databases are captured. Defaults to `true`; `false` needs `confirm_exclude_databases`.
- `persistent_volume_claims` (List of String) Volumes to capture, as `namespace/name`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imported by <cluster_id>/<stack_name>. retention and selection are not read back.
terraform import ankra_stack_backup_protection.shop 0b6f1d2e-1111-4222-8333-944445555666/shop
```
